Observation families supported by mvgam

Source: R/mvgam_families.R
mvgam_families.Rd

mvgam() and jsdgam() accept the observation families that brms and stats define. mvgam adds families for data that ecological and epidemiological series tend to produce. They cover counts observed with imperfect detection, compositions and counts whose dispersion a negative binomial cannot reach.

Pass a family as you would to brms::brm() or stats::glm(), for example mvgam(y ~ x, trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1), family = nmix()). The N-mixture article fits nmix(). The JSDM article fits a joint species distribution model.

Families mvgam adds

Each fixes its link. com_binomial() takes a link argument that accepts "logit" alone. The table lists every argument.

FamilyLinkArguments
tweedie()logM, the truncation point of the compound Poisson sum
beta_nb()lognone
com_binomial()logitlink, "logit" only
nmix()log (state), logit (detection)type, one of "poisson_binomial", "royle_nichols" or "poisson_poisson"; multi_season
occ()logit (state and detection)multi_season
diri()identitynone
multi()identitynone
categ()identitynone
mvn()identitynone
mvt()identitynone

Choosing by the shape of the response

Real-valued

stats::gaussian(), brms::student(), brms::skew_normal(), brms::exgaussian(), brms::asym_laplace() and brms::von_mises() for angles.

Non-negative real-valued

stats::Gamma(), brms::lognormal(), brms::exponential(), brms::weibull(), brms::frechet() and stats::inverse.gaussian(). tweedie() takes continuous data with a point mass at zero. With a trend, give these families link = "log". Their mean must stay positive. Under the identity, inverse or 1/mu^2 link it stays positive only where the linear predictor is positive on every row. A latent trend is centred near zero and takes negative values, where the likelihood is undefined. stats::Gamma() defaults to the inverse link. mvgam() warns when a trend meets one of these links. lognormal() is the exception. Its mu is a log-scale location that takes any sign. identity is the right link for it.

A single proportion on (0, 1)

Beta(), with brms::zero_inflated_beta() or brms::zero_one_inflated_beta() when the bounds are attainable.

Compositions and choices among categories

diri() for proportions summing to one, multi() for counts across categories and categ() for one chosen category per unit.

Binary

brms::bernoulli().

Counts out of a known number of trials

stats::binomial(). brms::beta_binomial() takes overdispersed trials. com_binomial() takes trials that are under- or over-dispersed.

Unbounded counts

stats::poisson(), brms::negbinomial(), brms::geometric() and their zero-inflated and hurdle counterparts (see brms::brmsfamily()). beta_nb() takes tails heavier than a negative binomial reaches.

Repeat visits to a site

nmix() estimates latent abundance from repeated counts. occ() estimates latent occupancy from repeated detection histories.

Several responses measured together

mvn() and mvt(), whose residual correlations come from a latent factor structure.

Ordered

brms::cumulative(), brms::sratio(), brms::cratio() and brms::acat().

Link functions

A brms or stats family takes a link argument as usual. poisson(link = "sqrt") and Gamma(link = "log") both work. mvgam writes the Stan code for the families in the table against one scale. Those families fix their link.

Data layout

nmix() and occ() are closure-unit families. They expect several rows per closure unit, one per visit. They model the state and the detection process with separate linear predictors. bf() supplies the second, as in bf(y ~ elev, p ~ tod). sim_closure_unit_data() simulates the layout they take. pivot_detection_array() reshapes a site-by-visit array into it. diri(), multi(), categ(), mvn() and mvt() also take several rows per unit, one per category or response.

What the family changes after fitting

A closure-unit family adds predict(type = "latent_state") and predict(type = "detection"). It supports pp_check(type = "fit_stat"). It refuses the pp_check() types that assume one observation per row.

brms::dirichlet(), brms::multinomial() and brms::categorical() are refused with a pointer to diri(), multi() and categ(). These fit the same responses in mvgam's long-format layout. brms::logistic_normal() is refused with a pointer to mvn(), which fits the additive log-ratios of the proportions.

See also

mvgam(), jsdgam(), brms::brmsfamily(), get_prior(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), sim_closure_unit_data()

Other observation families: beta_nb(), categ(), com_binomial(), diri(), multi(), mvn(), mvt(), nmix(), occ(), tweedie()

Examples

# Families are constructed, then passed to `family`
nmix(type = "royle_nichols")
#> 
#> Custom family: nmix_royle_nichols 
#> Link function: log 
#> Parameters: mu, p 
#> 
com_binomial()
#> 
#> Custom family: com_binomial 
#> Link function: logit 
#> Parameters: mu, nu 
#> 
tweedie(M = 40L)
#> 
#> Custom family: tweedie 
#> Link function: log 
#> Parameters: mu, mphi, mtheta 
#> 

# A brms or stats family still takes its own link
poisson(link = "sqrt")
#> 
#> Family: poisson 
#> Link function: sqrt 
#> 

# The layout occ() takes: one row per visit to each site
head(sim_closure_unit_data(family = occ())$data_train)
#>   visit site series time y cap        env      tod_c
#> 1     1    1   sp_1    1 1   1 -0.2228471  4.0020204
#> 2     2    1   sp_1    1 0   1 -0.2228471  4.6148115
#> 3     3    1   sp_1    1 1   1 -0.2228471  4.3712082
#> 4     4    1   sp_1    1 0   1 -0.2228471 -0.8113259
#> 5     1    2   sp_1    2 1   1 -0.3107994  2.2083795
#> 6     2    2   sp_1    2 0   1 -0.3107994  2.8288534
